subject: WellspringDX pilot: eval pilot setup, dataset format & scoring agreement
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@wellspringdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: WellspringDX pilot: eval pilot setup, dataset format & scoring agreement

Hi Caroline — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before marissa and I put the pilot SOW together.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: run a controlled model-fit pilot that evaluates Redwood-hosted inference for two major tasks: 1) clinical triage classification and 2) short free-text summarization for consult notes.
- Success criteria: match or beat current internal rule-based accuracy on triage (target: >= 88% F1) and produce summaries with mean human rating >= 4/5 on usefulness/accuracy.
- Timeline: 4-week trial (data ingest + eval run + scoring + feedback cycle).

Redwood recommended test matrix (initial)
- Model candidates: rw-instruct-7b-v2 (low-latency candidate), open-llama-13b-qdq (higher capacity), orca-mini-13b (balanced). We'll run each with your prompt bank and our standard temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) where applicable.
- Evaluation modes: deterministic scoring for classification (single prediction per prompt), n=5 sampling for summarization + human adjudication sample.

Immediate asks from Wellspring
1) A 200–500 row sample CSV (anonymized) for each task; required columns: id, prompt, expected_label (for triage), expected_summary (for summarization), category, patient_age_bucket, source_system, and notes. I attached a sample schema.
2) Any internal quality anchors or edge-case examples you want prioritized (e.g., rare diagnosis phrases).
3) Procurement contact for SOW/PO (I’ve cc’d procurement alias — please confirm preferred PO flow).

Attachments we uploaded for pilot prep
- wellspring_sample_dataset_schema.csv (CSV schema + toy rows)
- redwood_eval_template.jsonl (our scoring harness template you can view)
- draft pilot_sow-draft.pdf (SOW skeleton; not final)

Next steps (proposed)
- Caroline: send anonymized sample datasets by EOD Thursday (2/12).
- Redwood: we’ll provision a sandbox project, upload eval harness, and share a run plan by Friday (2/13).
- Schedule: 30–45m check-in after you drop data to finalize scoring buckets and acceptance thresholds.

If this looks right I’ll flag marissa to draft the SOW + timeline.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: WellspringDX pilot: eval pilot setup, dataset format & scoring agreement

Markus — quick internal notes / items for SOW and handoff to solutions:  

1) Model selection rationale to include in SOW:
- rw-instruct-7b-v2: lowest cost, should be primary baseline for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- open-llama-13b-qdq: expect better classification calibration, include quantized variant for cost gating.
- orca-mini-13b: good middle ground; include as tie-breaker for summarization.

2) Scoring framework (what we’ll deliver in pilot report):
- Classification: precision/recall/F1 by category + confusion matrix + threshold sensitivity analysis.
- Summarization: automated ROUGE-L for initial pass; normalized Levenshtein for exactness; 150-sample human rating (use our 1-5 rubric).
- Regression guardrails: store baseline logits and token-level diffs for top-2 models; flag >5% drop in F1 or >0.3 drop in mean human score across two consecutive runs.

3) Ops notes:
- Require an S3 presigned upload instructions (we’ll give a one-time ingestion key).
- Data retention: sandbox project will maintain data for 30 days by default; add option for extended retention in SOW.

4) Deliverables to include in pilot SOW:
- Eval runbook + scoring script (attached template)
- Summary report with per-model recommendations and cost/latency trade-offs
- Optional canary for production routing if results pass acceptance thresholds

I’ll pick up the SOW draft once markus confirms timeline. Ben — please queue a small demo env for the sandbox and ensure the template scoring harness is the one linked in the drive.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@wellspringdx.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Tan <kevin.tan@wellspringdx.com>, procurement@wellspringdx.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: WellspringDX pilot: eval pilot setup, dataset format & scoring agreement

Hi Markus / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We can get a sanitized sample to you by EOD Thursday. A couple clarifications from our side before we send: 

1) For the summarization task — expected_summary: should that be full clinician-style phrasing or a bullet list 'patient problem list' format? We have both variants in our corpus.
2) For the classification task — do you require a fixed label set? We currently have triage labels: emergent / urgent / routine / referral. We can map but want to confirm.
3) Scoring: our clinical QA lead wants to see the human-rating rubric ahead of time (so our raters are aligned). Can you send the rubric as a PDF or doc?

Procurement: Kevin, please confirm whether Wellspring prefers a single PO for the sandbox pilot or separate POs per milestone. Procurement — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Also attached is a tiny anonymized CSV (10 rows) so you can sanity-check the schema first.

Thanks,
Caroline Wu
Head of Clinical Product
Wellspring Diagnostics

Attachment: wellspring_10row_sample.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@wellspringdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@wellspringdx.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: WellspringDX pilot: eval pilot setup, dataset format & scoring agreement

Caroline — perfect, and thanks for the sample. Answers inline below and a concrete next step list.

1) Summarization format: please include both variants if possible. For scoring we'll run separate buckets: (A) clinician-style free-text and (B) problem-list bullets. We’ll evaluate each independently since the metric expectations differ. Note: for problem-list we expect higher exact-match rates, and for clinician-style we rely more on human ratings and ROUGE-L.

2) Labels: please use your native triage set (emergent / urgent / routine / referral). We will map if necessary but want to preserve your real labels for better calibration reporting. Include any label definitions as a short glossary column in the upload.

3) Human-rating rubric: attached (redwood_rubric_v1.pdf) — key points: 1-5 scale where 1 = harmful/incorrect, 3 = usable with edits, 5 = accurate and clinically useful. We will run a 150-sample double-blind rating for summarization and present inter-rater agreement (Krippendorff's alpha).

Operational details / timeline
- Thursday (2/12) EOD: Wellspring uploads full sample CSV(s) to S3 presigned link (we’ll send the link once procurement confirms PO flow).
- Friday (2/13): Redwood will spin up sandbox, ingest data, and run a small smoke eval with rw-instruct-7b-v2 to validate pipeline.
- Week of 2/16: Full pilot run across models; preliminary report by 2/23.

Acceptance thresholds (proposed; we can adjust post-smoke run)
- Triage classification: F1 >= 0.88 (macro) across top categories OR > 2% improvement over your baseline on key categories.
- Summarization: mean human rating >= 4.0 AND ROUGE-L >= 0.45 on clinician-style summaries.
- Regression guard: any model showing >5% drop in F1 vs baseline or >0.3 drop in mean human score triggers a pause + investigation.

Next steps for procurement & SOW
- Kevin / procurement: confirm purchase flow (single PO vs milestone POs) so we can finish SOW.
- Caroline: once full sample uploaded we’ll schedule a 30m alignment call (I’ll include a Calendly link in the SOW draft).

Attachments included in this thread:
- wellspring_sample_dataset_schema.csv (schema + toy rows)
- redwood_eval_template.jsonl (scoring harness template)
- pilot_sow-draft.pdf (SOW skeleton)
- redwood_rubric_v1.pdf (human rating rubric)

If that works I’ll have Marissa produce the final SOW and Ben will prepare the sandbox.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.

Markus Klein
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
